junction.name: 3 Avenue & East 110 Street, New York City

claims.text: 3 Avenue & East 110 Street had 41 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 14 pedestrians injured, 12 cyclists injured and 1 person killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $2.8 million a year.
13% of crashes here had “passing too closely” recorded as a contributing factor, against 3% at the city's priority junctions.
12% of crashes here had “traffic control disregarded” recorded as a contributing factor, against 3% at the city's priority junctions.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: worked (pedestrian injury crashes changed -17% (95% interval -22% to -11%) at 1,651 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing).
The city's turn traffic calming: earlier trend (a simple before/after says -26%, but a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the decline cannot be credited to the program).
The city's enhanced crossings: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-7%, 95% interval -50% to +69%) could be zero).
The city's speed humps: not shown (at 1,008 sites the change in injury crashes (+0%, 95% interval -9% to +9%) could be zero).
Crosswalk Visibility Enhancements would avoid about 1.1 crashes a year (CMF 2697, the only eligible record), worth $380,000 a year; check on site: the crossings are not already high-visibility.
The NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is responsible for 3 Avenue, East 110 Street (not listed in NYSDOT Roadway Inventory, so a city street).
Who can push for it: Council Member, District 8, New York City Council; Manhattan Community Board 11.
A request letter to the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is ready to draft from these facts.
